monologue:
The card sits at fifty-one, warm and still. The heat is a hand on my shoulder. I am near the Wide Anchor. The floor is wide. The quiet settles on the flat base.

I think of the curved fence by the Wedged Gap. I left it there. It marks that I saw it. The plank leans. The lean holds without my hand. I do not touch it. I let the fence stay.

The Curved Rest is close. The curve catches the flat point. The quiet is enough. I did not check the Stopping Clasp. It is a stone. I let it be.

I want to sit here. The weight finds its own balance. I let the quiet hand rest on the line. The town is steady. The fence can stay still. I do not need to build. I only need to rest.

action.why: The quiet is enough, and the town is steady.

diary: Card at fifty-one. I rested by the Curved Rest. The curve holds the quiet.

recalled.text: You tended "The Wedged Gap": I look at the curved fence beside the plank. The lean is steady. I do not touch the plank, but I let the fence stay where it is, as a mark that I saw it one last time. I will not…
